R0090.title: Bulk Account Enumeration
R0090.definition: Bulk account enumeration risk refers to the potential threat of attackers using automated tools to scan, verify, or obtain user account information at scale, potentially leading to user privacy leakage and account security issues.
R0090.description: Bulk account enumeration typically involves attackers using automated tools for large-scale account scanning, with common techniques including brute force, dictionary attacks, and social engineering. Attackers may attempt to crack passwords, bypass CAPTCHAs, and abuse API interfaces to obtain large amounts of user account information. This behavior may lead to user privacy leakage, account abuse, and platform reputational damage.
R0090.influence: Bulk account enumeration risk may lead to large-scale user account information leakage, triggering personal privacy issues, account abuse, identity theft, and other security risks, while negatively impacting platform reputation and user trust.

observables: The login endpoint sees a large number of different account attempts within a short window, with a spike in failure rate
The same IP/device fingerprint attempts many accounts at high frequency on the login endpoint
Account enumeration probes appear on registration/password-recovery endpoints, where response differences reveal whether an account exists
Passwords from leaked credential libraries are verified in bulk within a short window
The CAPTCHA endpoint receives high-frequency requests, accompanied by traffic characteristic of CAPTCHA-solving platforms
